'''Keita Bates-Diop''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|eɪ|t|ə|_|ˈ|b|eɪ|t|s|_|ˈ|d|iː|ɒ|p}} {{respell|KAY|tə|_|BAYTS|_|DEE|op}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> born January 23, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is currently an assistant coach for the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]].

Bates-Diop was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the 48th overall pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He spent 1 and a half seasons with Minnesota before getting traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in 2020, but only appeared in 7 games for Denver. Bates-Diop would then play for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] over the next three seasons before signing with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in 2023 as a free agent. Halfway through the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023-24 NBA season]], the Suns traded Bates-Diop to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in February of 2024 in a three team trade sending [[Royce O'Neale]] to Phoenix.

==Early life==
Keita Bates-Diop was born on January 23, 1996, in [[Sacramento, California]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.columbusalive.com/entertainment/20180307/keita-bates-diop-leads-rising-ohio-state-basketball-team|title=Keita Bates-Diop leads a rising Ohio State basketball team|access-date=March 7, 2018|date=March 7, 2018|website=columbusalive.com|author=Downing, Andy}}</ref> to Richard and Wilma Bates. His parents added Diop to his surname. His father Richard studied under [[Cheikh Anta Diop]], a Senegalese scientist and anthropologist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pantagraph.com/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/u-high-s-bates-diop-drawing-d-i-attention/article_5acba094-47ed-11e1-b92e-0019bb2963f4.html|title=U High's Bates-Diop drawing D-I attention|access-date=January 26, 2012|date=January 26, 2012|website=[[Pantagraph.com]]|author=Kindred, Randy}}</ref>

==High school career==
Bates-Diop played for [[University High School (Normal, Illinois)|University High School]] in [[Normal, Illinois]]. He averaged 18.4 points, 6.7 rebounds and 2.3 blocks as a junior. He was considered one of the top 5 candidates for Illinois Mr. Basketball by the [[Chicago Tribune]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2013/11/27/boys-hoops-top-5-mr-basketball-candidates/|title=Boys hoops – Top 5 Mr. Basketball candidates|access-date=January 31, 2014|date=November 27, 2013|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}}</ref> Bates-Diop was ranked no. 24 nationally in his class by [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2014/03/nik_stauskas_a_second-team_all.html|title=Michigan's Nik Stauskas gets All-America honor; recruit Kameron Chatman a prep All-American|access-date=March 12, 2014|date=March 10, 2014|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Baumgardner, Nick}}</ref>

==College career==
Bates-Diop was a bench player as a freshman at OSU in the 2014–15 season. As a sophomore, he expanded his role on the team and averaged 11.8 points and 6.4 rebounds per game.<ref name=markus/> But as a junior, he suffered a stress fracture in his left leg, sitting out all but the first nine games, while the Buckeyes limped to a 17–15 record without him. In those nine games, Bates-Diop averaged 9.7 points and 5.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news|last=Birdsong|first=Nick|title=Ohio State's Keita Bates-Diop is the difference maker the Buckeyes needed all along|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/ohio-state-buckeyes-basketball-schedule-roster-keita-bates-diop-2018-mock-draft-analysis/ro4ahghrqvq01scjf6x4zulkl|access-date=January 19, 2018|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=November 22, 2017|archive-date=January 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180120124713/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/ohio-state-buckeyes-basketball-schedule-roster-keita-bates-diop-2018-mock-draft-analysis/ro4ahghrqvq01scjf6x4zulkl|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was granted a medical redshirt and came into his redshirt junior campaign one of the top options for new coach [[Chris Holtmann]].<ref name=markus>{{cite news|last=Markus|first=Don|title=In order to beat Ohio State, Maryland has to stop Keita Bates-Diop|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2018/01/11/in-order-to-beat-ohio-state-maryland-has-to-stop-keita-bates-diop/|access-date=January 19, 2018|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=January 11, 2018|archive-date=February 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180209172602/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/tracking-the-terps/bs-sp-maryland-ohio-state-bates-diop-0111-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Bates-Diop earned his first [[Big Ten Conference]] player of the week honors on December 11, 2017, after notching a career-high 27 points in a 97–62 win over [[2017–18 William & Mary Tribe men's basketball team|William & Mary]].<ref name=MSOSEWMBY>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/121117aac.html|title=Michigan State, Ohio State Earn Weekly Men's Basketball Honors: Buckeyes' Keita Bates-Diop earns Player of the Week award; Spartans' Jaren Jackson Jr. named Freshman of the Week|access-date=December 11, 2017|date=December 11, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=BigTen.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171212193053/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/121117aac.html|archive-date=December 12, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 9, 2018, Bates-Diop was recognized as the Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] after strong performances against [[2017–18 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] and [[2017–18 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. Bates-Diop tied a then-career high with 27 points and grabbed 13 rebounds in a victory against Iowa. Against top-ranked Michigan State, he scored a career-high 32 points in an 80–64 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2018/oscar180109.html|title=Ohio State's Bates-Diop Is Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week|access-date=January 19, 2018|date=January 9, 2018|publisher=The [[United States Basketball Writers Association]]}}</ref> He also received his second Big Ten player of the week recognition.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/010818aag.html|title=Maryland, Ohio State Earn Weekly Men's Basketball Honors: Buckeyes' Keita Bates-Diop earns Player of the Week award; Terrapins' Bruno Fernando named Freshman of the Week|website=[[Big Ten Conference]]|language=en|access-date=January 8, 2018|date=January 8, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180109063608/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/010818aag.html|archive-date=January 9, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> Bates-Diop received his second consecutive player of the week nod on January 15, with a 26-point, eight-rebound outing in a 91–69 win over [[2017–18 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]] and 20 points and nine rebounds in a victory versus [[2017–18 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/011518aad.html|title=Michigan State, Ohio State Earn Weekly Men's Basketball Honors: Buckeyes' Keita Bates-Diop earns second-consecutive Player of the Week award; Spartans' Jaren Jackson Jr. named Freshman of the Week for third time|website=[[Big Ten Conference]]|language=en|access-date=January 15, 2018|date=January 15, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116005906/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/011518aad.html|archive-date=January 16, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On February 26, 2018, Bates-Diop was named the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022618aad.html |title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN |date=February 26, 2018 |access-date=February 26, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180227094314/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022618aad.html |archive-date=February 27, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He averaged 19.8 points and 8.7 rebounds per game. Following Ohio State's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Bates-Diop announced his intention to forgo his final season of collegiate eligibility and declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=March 26, 2018 |title=Buckeyes forward Keita Bates-Diop to enter NBA draft |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22916723 |access-date=March 26, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Minnesota Timberwolves / Iowa Wolves (2018–2020)===
On June 21, 2018, Bates-Diop was drafted by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the 48th pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2018/06/ohio_states_keita_bates-diop_s.html|title=Keita Bates-Diop selected in second round, No. 48 overall by Minnesota Timberwolves in 2018 NBA Draft|last=Landis|first=Bill|date=June 21, 2018|work=Cleveland.com|access-date=June 22, 2018}}</ref> On July 7, 2018, he signed with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 7, 2018 |title=Timberwolves Sign Keita Bates-Diop |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-keita-bates-diop |access-date=July 7, 2018 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Bates-Diop participated in the [[NBA Summer League]] in 2018 and 2019.

===Denver Nuggets / Windy City Bulls (2020)===
On February 5, 2020, the Timberwolves traded Bates-Diop to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in a four-team trade.<ref>{{cite web |title=Denver Nuggets Acquire Bates-Diop, Napier, Vonleh, Green and First-Round Pick in Four-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-four-team-trade-020520a |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 6, 2020 |date=February 5, 2020}}</ref> He was assigned to the [[Windy City Bulls]] on March 1.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nuggets' Keita Bates-Diop: Sent to G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nuggets-keita-bates-diop-sent-to-g-league/ |access-date=March 2, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 1, 2020}}</ref> He was waived by the Nuggets on November 22, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=NBA Player Transactions|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/transactions/#|website=NBA.com |access-date=November 26, 2020 |date=February 26, 2020}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2020–2023)===
On November 29, 2020, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] announced that they had signed Bates-Diop to a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Pederson |first=Landon |date=November 29, 2020 |title=Spurs sign Keita Bates-Diop to two-way contract |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-keita-bates-diop-two-way-contract |access-date=November 29, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On September 7, 2021, the Spurs re-signed Bates-Diop to a two-year, $3.6 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mauricio |first=Ezekiel |date=September 7, 2021 |title=Spurs re-sign Keita Bates-Diop |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-re-sign-keita-bates-diop |access-date=September 7, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 23, 2021, Bates-Diop scored a career-high 30 points on 11-of-11 shooting with seven rebounds and a steal in a 138–110 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 23, 2021 |title=Spurs rout depleted Lakers 138–110 in last Staples game |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401360311 |access-date=December 23, 2021 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2023–2024)===
On July 4, 2023, Bates-Diop signed a two-year, $5 million contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web |date=July 4, 2023 |title=Suns Sign Keita Bates-Diop, Drew Eubanks, Chimezie Metu and Yuta Watanabe |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-keita-bates-diop-drew-eubanks-chimezie-metu-and-yuta-watanabe |access-date=July 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2024)===
On February 8, 2024, Bates-Diop was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Three-Team Trade with Phoenix and Memphis|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-complete-three-team-trade-with-phoenix-and-memphis|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref> On March 27, 2024, the Nets announced that Bates-Diop would miss the rest of the season due to a fractured tibia.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nets Notebook: Keita Bates-Diop ruled out for season due to fracture in tibia|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2024/03/27/nets-keita-bated-diop-out-for-season-raptors/|work=New York Daily News|date=March 27, 2024|access-date=June 3, 2024}}</ref>

On July 6, 2024, Bates-Diop was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] alongside [[Mikal Bridges]] and one second-round pick in exchange for [[Bojan Bogdanović]], [[Mamadi Diakite]], [[Shake Milton]], 4 unprotected first-round picks, an unprotected pick swap, a top four protected first round pick, and an unprotected second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Acquire Mikal Bridges and Keita Bates-Diop|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/mikal-bridges-acquired-in-trade-with-brooklyn-nets|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}}</ref> Before ever appearing in a game for the Knicks, on October 2, 2024, Bates-Diop was traded back to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in a three team trade involving the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in which Minnesota also acquired [[Donte DiVincenzo]], [[Julius Randle]], and one Lottery Protected first-round pick. The Hornets received [[DaQuan Jeffries]], [[Charlie Brown Jr. (basketball)|Charlie Brown Jr.]], [[Duane Washington Jr.]], three second-round picks and draft compensation. New York acquired [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] and the draft rights to [[James Nnaji]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Nardinger|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Forward Keita Bates-Diop, Guard Donte DiVincenzo and Forward Julius Randle from New York Knicks|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-forward-keita-bates-diop-guard-donte-divincenzo-and-forward-julius-randle-from-new-york-knicks|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=October 2, 2024}}</ref> On October 21, he was waived by the Timberwolves after playing only two preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Stanton|title=Timberwolves Finalize 2024-25 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-finalize-2024-25-opening-night-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}}</ref>

===Qingdao Eagles (2025)===
On February 20, 2025, Bates-Diop signed with the [[Qingdao Eagles]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{cite web |title=青岛男篮官宣凯塔·贝兹·迪奥普加盟 |url=https://www.qdxin.cn/sports/2025/355329.html |website=信网 |access-date=February 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250220085257/https://www.qdxin.cn/sports/2025/355329.html |archive-date=February 20, 2025 |date=February 20, 2025 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Coaching career ==
On October 23, 2025, Bates-Diop was hired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League]] as an assistant coach, despite not announcing his retirement.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Skyforce Announces Coaching Staff Editions |url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-coaching-staff-editions |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=Sioux Falls Skyforce |language=en}}</ref>
